ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every director, member, representative, and ultimate beneficial owner of the Yuhan Hoesa must be screened before onboarding against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN and non-SDN consolidated lists, the UK HMT sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea's sanctions designations under the Act on Prohibition of Financing for Terrorist Activities. KOFIU guidance requires risk-based customer due diligence that traces ownership through all legal layers to natural persons at the 25-percent threshold, applies enhanced due diligence to politically exposed persons and their family members and close associates, validates source of funds for paid-in capital, and requires proactive filing of suspicious transaction reports to KOFIU. Screening data must be refreshed every 90 days and records preserved for at least five years after termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr) and the Court Registration Information System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Yuhan Hoesa must have a Hangul trade name that ends with Yuhan Hoesa as the corporate form suffix. Foreign-language terms may be used only if Hangul phonetic equivalency is established in the register; the name must be clearly distinguishable from other companies in the same business object. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) distinctive descriptive brand; (2) business object or industry indicator; (3) corporate form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) absence of any prohibited or restricted token. An English name may be used in parallel contracts, but the Korean registry name is the controlling legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be contested by filing a written objection with the registration judge of the competent district court within seven days under the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act. The objection must attach the name-search result from the Internet Registration Office, a comparison table with the cited conflicting entity, and arguments on visual, phonetic, and semantic distinction. No extension of the statutory seven-day objection period is permitted. If the objection is dismissed, or the single 30-day name reservation lapses, the applicant must refile through the Internet Registration Office with a revised Hangul trade name and pay a new registration fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox address is materially rejected by the National Tax Service and Korean banks for this industry. Under Articles 6 and 7 of the Enforcement Decree of the Corporate Tax Act and the VAT Act, the registered head office must be a physical place where management is exercised, accounting records and corporate registers are kept, and tax invoices are issued. Banks applying FATF, OFAC, and KOFIU customer due diligence standards require proof of physical occupancy, a lease agreement under the company name, utility contracts, and often a site visit. A virtual-office address that receives mail but lacks substantive business operations will trigger enhanced scrutiny or account-opening refusal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for on-site inspection: 1) company nameplate at the registered office; 2) lease agreement and rent deposit receipt in the legal entity's name; 3) utility bill and building access log; 4) physical stock or raw materials consistent with food-grade silicone compression molding; 5) tax invoices, VAT records, and accounting ledgers; and 6) presence of a responsible officer or employee. Quantified risk: moderate, approximately 40% chance of an unannounced district tax office visit within the first 12 months, and 15% chance of a registry verification visit for a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa without prior corporate tax history.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, promulgated 27 December 1962, as amended), Part 4, Articles 287-2 through 287-74 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), together with the Commercial Registration Act, the Regulation on Commercial Registration, and the Notary Public Act for certification of the Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the principal place of business of the Yuhan Hoesa, with electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) and in-person filing at the court registry counter.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), submitted with the certified notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital payment certificate, the subscription and contribution schedule, the consent and appointment forms of the statutory officers, and the registered office consent documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, the Articles of Incorporation must state the aggregate amount of member contributions and each member's subscription amount. All cash contributions must be fully deposited into a temporary Korean bank account opened in the name of the company in formation before the incorporation registration application is filed, and the bank must issue a valid capital payment certificate or balance confirmation. Contributions in kind must be appraised by an independent appraiser, and the appraisal record must be attached to the registration file. No blocked escrow account is required beyond the statutory restriction that contributed funds may not be withdrawn before the legal personality of the company arises.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA, a limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, on [DATE], at [TIME] Korean Standard Time, at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], by unanimous written consent in lieu of a formal meeting.

WHEREAS, the Members have subscribed to the contribution amounts set out in the Articles of Incorporation and have fully paid such contributions into a bank account opened for the company in formation; and

WHEREAS, all directors and the auditor, if any, have been lawfully elected or appointed and have accepted their positions; and

WHEREAS, the registered office of the Company will be located in the Republic of Korea for submission to the Registry.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. The subscription schedule set out in the Articles of Incorporation, including all cash and in-kind contributions, is hereby ratified, confirmed, and accepted by the Board, and the capital payment certificate issued by [BANK NAME] dated [DATE] is approved as conclusive evidence of capital payment in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Commercial Act.

2. The registered office address of the Company is hereby fixed at [FULL STREET ADDRESS], Republic of Korea. The Managing Director is authorized to execute the lease agreement and to take all actions necessary to record the registered office in the commercial register with the competent District Court.

3. The Board approves the opening of corporate banking accounts with [BANK NAME], the use of SWIFT TT and platform-pay rails in accordance with the Company's payment model, and confirms that all bank mandates, online banking security forms, payment service agreements, and foreign exchange documents are authorized.

4. The following persons are hereby appointed as statutory officers: [NAME] as Managing Director, [NAME] as Director, and [NAME] as Auditor if legally required. Each statutory officer shall have the full authority, actual or apparent, to perform the duties assigned by law and by the Articles of Incorporation.

5. The Managing Director is expressly authorized to file all tax registrations, factory establishment permits, environmental applications, and product safety confirmations, and to execute contracts for the manufacture, warehousing, and sale of food-grade silicone tactile sensory fidgets under ISIC 3240.

6. The corporate seal of the Company is hereby adopted, and the Managing Director is directed to register the seal with the competent District Court and the tax authority.

7. These resolutions are effective immediately upon the Company's incorporation registration and shall be recorded in the Board resolution book.

Dated and adopted on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Review, Business Scope Validation, and Drafting of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) for name conflict search; Korean Intellectual Property Office for trademark search; notary public for legal drafting review; local municipal zoning office for land-use confirmation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name conflict search for the proposed Korean corporate name and, if a foreign-language trade name is intended, review the Korean Intellectual Property Office trademark search database. Confirm that the proposed registered office address is lawfully usable as a factory or office address for toy manufacturing under the National Land Planning and Utilization Act. Prepare a draft of the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, containing the corporate name, the aggregate member contributions, the names and details of each member, the number and identity of the directors, a precise business purpose covering the compression molding of food-grade silicone tactile sensory fidgets, storage, wholesale, and export, the registered office location, the accounting period, and the method of dissolution. Circulate corporate governance disclosures to each proposed member, director, and auditor, and collect identity documents and consents before notarization.
required_dossiers: Proposed Korean and English company names
Passport or government-issued photographic identification of each proposed member and director
Proof of address or lease interest in the intended registered office
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Completed conflicts and trademark search reports
Consent forms of each proposed statutory officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected by the registry or trademark database, select an alternate Korean name and re-run the conflict search before proceeding. If the zoning use is not permitted for toy manufacturing, identify a lawful alternate registered office address and update the draft Articles of Incorporation accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Deposit and Bank Payment Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank branch capable of issuing a capital payment certificate for a company in formation; for in-kind contributions, an independent licensed appraiser.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the member subscriptions are closed, all cash contributions must be deposited to a temporary bank account opened in the name of Yuhang Hoesa (in formation) at a Korean commercial bank. Each member's transfer instruction must identify the payor as the contributor named in the Articles of Incorporation. The bank will execute a formation account agreement and, upon credit of funds, issue a deposit certificate or balance confirmation with a stamped branch signature. This certificate, showing the account title, deposit date, and amount, must remain outstanding through the registration submission. In-kind contributions are forbidden unless supported by a written appraisal in Korean prepared by an independent appraiser, and the appraisal records must be attached to the registration file. Do not withdraw contributed funds before legal personality is obtained.
required_dossiers: Temporary formation account application form
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Passport or government-issued identification of each paying member
Member contribution schedule detailing each subscription amount
Capital payment certificate or balance confirmation issued by the bank
In-kind contribution appraisal report and consent statement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate because of a mismatch in the member name or contribution amount, submit a corrected transfer in the exact registered name or execute a supplementary member resolution to amend the contribution schedule, then obtain a fresh certificate. If the bank suspects withdrawal or improper use of funds, provide a written undertaking that no funds will be withdrawn before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Authentication of Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public operating under the Notary Public Act at the jurisdiction chosen by the incorporators.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All members must attend a Korean notary public for certification of the Articles of Incorporation and for any authentication required by the Commercial Registration Act. The notary will verify the identity of each member, confirm that each has signed and consented to the Articles, and confirm the attached capital payment certificate. The notary will then certify the Articles by executing a notarial certificate of authentication. At least three notarized copies should be obtained: one for the District Court registry, one for the National Tax Service business registration, and one for the corporate record book. If a member or director resides abroad, a valid passport copy and apostilled or consular-verified evidence of legality and eligibility shall be submitted. The notarization step must be completed before the incorporation registration filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized final draft of the Articles of Incorporation
Capital payment certificate issued under Step 2
Passport or government-issued identification of each member and director
Power of attorney, if a member will be represented
Apostilled or consular-verified identity and eligibility documents for foreign participants
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the eligibility of a director or the valuation of a contribution in kind, furnish a criminal record certificate, an amended appraisal, or a supplement to the Articles of Incorporation and return to the notary for a fresh authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) or physical submission at the court registry counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, either through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office or at the registration counter. The application must include the certified Articles of Incorporation, the capital payment certificate, the subscription statement, the consent and appointment forms of the directors, the acceptance of the auditor, and the registered office consent documentation. At the same time, the registration fee and the local registration tax must be paid in the amount calculated by the registry. After judicial review, the registry will issue the corporate registration certificate and registration abstract, and the company is deemed incorporated under the Commercial Act from that moment. If the court issues a correction direction, cure the flaw and re-submit within the deadline before the application is abandoned.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital payment certificate and deposit confirmation
Statement of payment and subscription of member contributions
Consent and appointment forms of directors
Acceptance of appointment by auditor, if any
Registered office consent document, lease, or title evidence
Corporate seal impression and seal registration report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, prepare and submit the corrected document to the designated registry officer within the stated response window. If the application is rejected due to missing consent or seal documentation, obtain a written confirmation from the affected party, pay the revised fee if any, and refile the complete package on the IRO portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration, Corporate Seal Registration, and Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (HomeTax portal) and the local district tax office; the Registration Division of the District Court for corporate seal registration; National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Employment and Labor Office for social insurance and labor registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the corporate registration certificate is issued, register the business with the National Tax Service using the HomeTax portal within the statutory period after business commencement, identifying the principal business as the manufacturing of toys and silicone novelty products. Register the corporate seal with the District Court registry and, if necessary, with the municipal authority, and obtain a certificate of seal registration. Thereafter, activate the bank account in the company's name using the corporate registration abstract and seal certificate, enroll the employees in the national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance programs, and file the opening report for the physical factory location with the competent local authority under the factory establishment rules. The business registration certificate must show the manufacturing and wholesale activities relevant to ISIC 3240.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration (corporate registration abstract)
Copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form on HomeTax
Lease agreement or proof of registered office address
Corporate seal certificate and corporate seal impression
Passport or identification of the Managing Director
Bank account activation documentation
Employee roster and social insurance enrollment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service asks for proof of an actual physical place of business, submit a lease certificate, utility bill, or site photograph. If social insurance enrollment is delayed because of missing domestic identification, use the extraterritorial registration procedures available through the integrated social insurance portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), Korean Agency for Technology and Standards (KATS), Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), and the competent municipal authority (Si/Gun/Gu) administering factory establishment and environmental permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment Permit (Gongjang Seollip Heoga) and Safety Confirmation of Children's Products (Toy Safety) under the Children's Product Safety Special Act, plus Food Contact Silicone Compliance Notification under the Food Sanitation Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal HomeTax at www.hometax.go.kr. Customs-related export clearances are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the foreign non-resident entity creates a Korean permanent establishment (fixed place of business) or conducts taxable supplies through a local agent. For VAT purposes, any foreign enterprise supplying taxable goods or services in Korea (including via cross-border e-commerce) must register for VAT regardless of turnover. Step 2: If a domestic establishment exists, register the place of business with the competent district tax office by filing an 'Application for Business Registration' through HomeTax or in person. For a branch or subsidiary, submit certified Korean translations of the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, corporate resolution authorizing local registration, and a power of attorney appointing a domestic tax representative or paying agent. Step 3: If no domestic establishment exists, the foreign entity must appoint a domestic tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes, who will file the registration application on behalf of the entity. Step 4: The NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) that simultaneously serves as the Tax Identification Number (TIN) for both Corporate Income Tax and Value Added Tax purposes. Registration is typically completed within 3-5 business days. Step 5: After registration, the entity must activate its e-tax invoice issuance capability (via HomeTax or an NTS-certified ERP/API connector), register a cash receipt device if needed, and comply with periodic VAT filing and payment obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None comparable to the U.S. check-the-box election. The Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is statutorily classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act and is subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income (subject to territorial limitations for foreign-source income under tax treaties). Available statutory elections include: (i) simplified taxation for SMEs with annual turnover below the statutory threshold (currently KRW 80 million), which affects VAT calculation mechanics but does not change the entity-level income tax classification; (ii) consolidated corporate tax filing for domestic business groups meeting the criteria under the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination; (iii) tax incentive elections under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act for new growth industries; and (iv) hybrid mismatch elections are not permitted under domestic law; however, the Korean tax authorities apply OECD BEPS Action 2 recommendations when assessing cross-border hybrid arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum economic turnover threshold exists. A person or entity supplying taxable goods or services in Korea (including foreign non-resident suppliers) is mandatorily required to register for VAT upon commencement of any taxable business activity. Failure to register subjects the entity to penalty taxation and automatic assessment on deemed supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) through the NTS HomeTax system for all B2B supplies. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for every VAT taxpayer, regardless of annual turnover, since 1 January 2014. Each e-tax invoice must contain a digital signature, unique invoice number, and a machine-readable QR/code, and must be transmitted near-real-time (within 1 day after the supply date) to the NTS via the HomeTax API or certified fiscal intermediary. For B2C retail transactions, a cash receipt must be issued when requested or when the transaction value exceeds the statutory threshold; these are cleared through the NTS real-time cash receipt system. Integrated tax clearance requires the use of NTS-certified e-invoice API connectors or HomeTax Mini/Plus for real-time data submission; the system provides an anti-fraud digital stamping feature that verifies the authenticity and integrity of each invoice. Export zero-rated invoices require linkage with the KCS UNI-PASS export declaration system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value Added Tax Act, exports of goods are zero-rated if the goods leave the territory of Korea under a customs export declaration. Qualifying categories include: (i) direct export of goods sold to foreign buyers where the goods are consigned or transported from Korea; (ii) export on consignment or outward processing; (iii) sale of goods to foreign businesses if the goods are moved under the Korean customs bond system; (iv) international transport services, and specified intangible/digital services supplied to non-residents (including software and SaaS) as enumerated in the Presidential Enforcement Decree. To claim the 0% rate, the taxpayer must hold valid evidence that the goods were physically exported or that services were beneficially supplied to a non-resident, and that the sales consideration was received from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate) issued by the Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill) evidencing physical export and carrier endorsement
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Bank Receipt / Foreign Exchange Sale Certificate proving receipt of the export proceeds from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to strict audit by the National Tax Service under the VAT refund and exemption verification framework, with cross-checks against KCS customs data and bank foreign exchange records. If the required export documents are missing, incomplete, or otherwise non-compliant, the NTS will retroactively assess the 10% VAT on the supply, plus an underpayment penalty calculation per the Framework Act on National Taxes (generally 10% for late payment, 20-30% for improper reporting, and up to 40% for fraudulent underreporting). The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes a penalty of up to 5% of the un-repatriated amount for failing to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days (with possible extension granted under prior approval). In cases of fraudulent export zero-rating or forged documentation, criminal liability may arise, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 100 million, and the entire zero-rated benefit is clawed back with statutory interest. Persistently non-repatriated proceeds may trigger the reversal of zero-rating and the treatment of the supply as taxable domestic sale, with retroactive assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) for central bank oversight and the Foreign Exchange Information Network reporting duty, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the administrative authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a fundamentally liberalized but transaction-based foreign exchange control regime. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act applies a negative-list approach: transactions in both the current account and the capital account are permitted unless specifically prohibited, notified, or reported. The Korean won is convertible for legitimate trade and investment, but it is not a freely deliverable offshore currency for speculative corporate flows; non-residents cannot create unrecorded KRW liquidity, and every cross-border payment must be classified and filed through an authorized foreign exchange bank. For the Yuhan Hoesa, current account transactions such as export collections for silicone fidget toys, platform-based marketplace payouts, and import payments for raw silicone are generally unrestricted and can be executed under ordinary trade documents and purpose codes. Capital account transactions, including the initial non-resident shareholder capital injection, intercompany financing, and future dividend remittances, require prior foreign investment reporting or registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and are subject to bank compliance review; however, they are not subject to blanket convertibility prohibitions. Dividend remittance is possible after corporate income tax filings and retained earnings verification, but a 22% withholding tax under domestic tax law and a foreign exchange declaration will apply. The practical convertibility constraint is not the absence of hard currency but the high granularity of reporting: each inbound and outbound leg needs a purpose code, underlying contract, customs or trade evidence, and economic substance. The Bank of Korea aggregates cross-border settlement data through the Foreign Exchange Information Network, so banks will reject transactions without complete dossiers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Trade Regulations, export proceeds from the silicone fidget toy business must be collected through a registered foreign exchange bank within six months from the date of the Korea Customs Service export declaration or the date on which the goods are shipped, whichever is evidenced by the customs record. There is no mandatory surrender to the Bank of Korea and no mandatory conversion ratio; 0% of export proceeds must be converted to KRW. Exporters may hold the foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account and later convert at market rates when making KRW payments. If the proceeds are converted, the bank records the foreign exchange purchase in the Foreign Exchange Information Network. If collection cannot be completed within the six-month statutory timeline, the company must submit a written application for extension to the foreign exchange bank, supported by evidence of buyer default, trade disputes, customs delays, or other justifiable reasons. Failure to receive export proceeds within the prescribed period or to file an extension can lead to administrative fines and interruption of the company's foreign exchange bank relationship.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: KRW Corporate Settlement Account and Foreign Currency Deposit Account under FIPA Capital Escrow
Foreign Currency Trade Account, KRW Operating Account, and Export Collection Account
KRW Current Account and Foreign Currency Capital Account for Inbound Foreign Direct Investment
Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Investment and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail. Offshore fintech EMIs are not licensed under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act to operate domestic KRW accounts, local payment collections, VAT/tax clearing, or statutory foreign exchange reporting in Korea. An offshore EMI cannot legally serve as the Yuhan Hoesa's corporate settlement bank because it cannot interface with the Korean Real Name Financial Transactions Act, cannot file Foreign Exchange Information Network declarations on the company's behalf, and cannot issue FIPA capital verification documents. EMI and platform payment products may be used only as supplementary front-ends for marketplace sales if the ultimate settlement is routed into a Tier-1 Korean bank account; otherwise, they expose the company to unregistered foreign exchange collection and adverse AML ratings.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the statutory director and beneficial owner during initial corporate account onboarding. Remote consular proxy opening is not available for a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident ownership under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and FATF-aligned Korean AML requirements. The director, or a board-authorized executive with prior notification to the bank, must appear in person at a domestic branch, provide original valid passport(s), apostilled corporate registration and constitutional documents, a corporate seal certificate or equivalent, and undergo biometric verification. After initial onboarding, additional signatories and agents may be authenticated through a notarized and apostilled power of attorney with bank-countered specimen signatures, but the initial KYC interview cannot be waived.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and non-resident shareholder chain contains an offshore intermediary or tax-transparent entity, causing the bank to classify the relationship as opaque ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Korean Business Registration Certificate and corporate register extract; apostilled Articles of Incorporation/Memorandum and full share ledger; complete UBO chart down to every natural person with 25% or more equity; notarized passport copies; executive domicile proof; source-of-wealth statement with supporting investment, sale, or employment documents; and, if an intermediary holding company exists, its audited financial statements, board resolution, and ultimate beneficial ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First inbound capital injection is routed from a bank account in the name of a third party, not the declared shareholder, raising a third-party funding or illegal receivable red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements from the remitting account; shareholder resolution confirming the share capital subscription; declaration explaining the remittance route and the relationship of any third-party payer; underlying loan, gift, or asset-sale agreements proving legitimate source of funds; a written no-nominating-letter indemnity; and a signed certification to the receiving Korean bank that the transaction will be reported under the Foreign Exchange Information Network as FIPA capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Silicone fidget toy product scope is under-described, creating a risk of product misclassification as a medical device, toy with import safety compliance issues, or dual-use commodity with sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product specification and packaging line images; ISO 9001 quality management certificate, food-grade silicone compliance certificates from KTR, KCL, or an international testing body (LFGB or FDA 21 CFR 177.2600); HS code mapping with ISIC 3240 and NAICS 339930; end-use and end-customer declaration; supply chain invoices covering silicone pellets and molds; export order master list; and a signed product compliance statement confirming no medical, military, or sanctioned end use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marketplace-based platform pay settlements will arrive in fragmented tranches with buyer names that do not match export trade invoices, causing the bank to see irregular collections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full seller dashboard transaction history; platform monthly settlement reports; reconciliation schedule linking each settlement to the corresponding Korea Customs Service export declaration through UNI-PASS; warehouse dispatch log; refund/chargeback records; and a monthly foreign exchange declaration mapping each inward remittance to the proper trade proceeds purpose code.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial non-resident capital injection, the shareholder must file a foreign investment report with KOTRA or a designated domestic foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before or within a permissible window around the remittance. The capital wire must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 to the Yuhan Hoesa's FIPA foreign currency capital account at the selected Tier-1 Korean bank, using the exact shareholder name as on the foreign investment report, the finance purpose code for foreign direct investment, and the foreign investment confirmation number in the remittance reference field. Upon receipt, the bank verifies that the ordering customer matches the foreign investor, issues a foreign currency deposit receipt, and converts the funds into KRW at the market exchange rate before transfer to the KRW operating account. Capital verification for the Korean LLC is completed through the bank's balance certificate, the FIPA registration certificate, and, if applicable, a statutory auditor's certificate; the bank records the conversion in the Foreign Exchange Information Network. No surrender of KRW is required, but the capital account must be used only for the declared business purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For raw silicone and packaging purchases, the company will execute SWIFT MT103 payments from its KRW operating account after converting to USD or CNY at a registered Korean foreign exchange bank. For high-value equipment and tooling imports, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (sight or usance) issued by the Korean bank is the recommended clearing rail, with a confirming or advising bank abroad. For smaller, recurring raw-material purchases, documentary collections provide a lower-cost alternative, while royalties, warehouse service fees, and platform commissions should be settled by MT103 with the appropriate current account purpose code. Each outbound disbursement must be supported by the import declaration, supplier invoice, purchase order, bill of lading or airway bill, and customs clearance evidence, and the bank must file the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information Network before the payment can clear.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/KRW forward contracts at a Tier-1 Korean bank ring-fenced by confirmed export sales or import purchase orders
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps to manage mismatches between foreign currency trade receipts and KRW operating obligations
FX options purchased from a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank to hedge identifiable outstanding trade invoices; selling or writing options is restricted

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in the onshore won market are not permitted for the Yuhan Hoesa as a domestic corporate treasury tool; offshore NDFs are limited to non-resident financial counterparties and are therefore outside the allowable hedging perimeter

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return together with the approved financial statements for the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end (by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); a one-month extension is available upon filing an application of extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid corporate income tax; additional penalty of 20% if the return is not filed within six months after the due date; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% accrues on unpaid tax until settled; persistent delinquent filing exposes the entity to forced assessment, asset seizure, and ultimately administrative strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting approval of annual financial statements and internal registration of resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company register and statutory minutes maintained at the registered office (not routinely lodged with a government filing fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The meeting must be convened within three months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic cash fine is imposed solely for late meeting convention, but continued default allows minority holders to petition the court for inspection, provisional disposition, or, in extreme cases, judicial dissolution; failing to finalise the financial statements by the required deadline also strengthens NTS penalties in the related corporate tax filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified audit report and audited financial statements filing (for companies exceeding statutory audit thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (via the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System) and National Tax Service as an appendix to the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be approved at the ordinary general meeting and submitted to the National Tax Service with the corporate tax return; the audit report must be filed with the Financial Supervisory Service within seven working days from approval of the general meeting, in no case later than the extended corporate tax return due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor and submit the audit report triggers administrative fines of up to KRW 30,000,000 under the External Audit Act, demerits against the auditor’s licence, and disqualification from tax-credit benefits; sustained non-compliance can lead to designation of mandatory external audit by the regulator and penalisation of the representative director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business and occupation tax / ancillary municipal filing on annual gross revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District tax office (local government) having jurisdiction over the registered office address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, as prescribed by the local tax ordinance, generally by May 31 for the immediately preceding calendar year’s gross revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local tax accrues a 3% delinquent surcharge plus daily arrearage interest of approximately 0.02% to 0.03%; continued default enables the municipal authority to seize bank accounts, attach property, and publish the company as a delinquent taxpayer, ultimately leading to cancellation of the business trading licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies, etc. and its Presidential Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to obtain an independent audit by a certified public accountant if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, it meets any of the following quantitative triggers: (a) total balance-sheet assets are at least KRW 12 billion (about USD 9 million); (b) annual total revenue or turnover is at least KRW 10 billion (about USD 7.5 million); or (c) it has one hundred or more full-time employees on average. Additional triggers apply for companies designated by the Financial Services Commission because of public-interest risk or likely damage to creditors; below these thresholds the entity may prepare un-audited statutory financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies subject to statutory external audit; non-audited Yuhan Hoesa entities may elect to apply Korean GAAP for non-public enterprises (General Enterprise Accounting Standards / SME accounting standards).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Yuhan Hoesa is required to maintain a current register of members and to annually confirm its ultimate beneficial ownership information for the purposes of tax filings, banking relationships, and anti-money-laundering compliance. Although there is no separate public UBO filing obligation for private limited companies in Korea, any transfer of membership quotas or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the competent registry office and the National Tax Service within 30 days of the transaction. The company must also conduct an internal annual confirmation of the beneficial owner list and retain supporting evidence for seven years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for a registered office service provider or licensed corporate agent in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 30,000 per year for a certified CPA audit, depending on balance-sheet size, transaction volume, and statutory deadlines

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea's headline corporate income tax rate is 25% on the top tax bracket. However, the effective rate is reduced via progressive brackets: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 21% on income between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion; and 25% on income exceeding KRW 300 billion. A 10% surtax applies to corporate income tax for taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion. Incentives include the Tax Credit for R&D and Human Resources Development, special tax credits for facility investment, Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays for eligible foreign-invested high-tech businesses, Free Economic Zone incentives (50% corporate tax reduction for 3 years, followed by 50% reduction for 2 years), and a 20% exclusion of qualifying IP income (Patent Box-like regime). SME additional deductions for R&D up to 30-50% of qualifying expenses are available if the entity meets SME thresholds under the Framework Act on SMEs. For the silicone fidget manufacturing entity, any R&D in product design or manufacturing may qualify for SME R&D credits if properly documented.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NTS HomeTax System (홈택스), Corporate Income Tax Return Form (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서), Form No. 101 (법인세법 제60조), filed with the competent district tax office. E-filing is mandatory for all corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers). A one-month extension is available upon application for foreign-invested companies and foreign-controlled entities; an additional extension of up to 60 days is available for corporations with overseas branches. An extension must be filed with Form No. 102 before the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the 10-digit Korean business registration number of the Yuhan Hoesa. If the entity is a foreign-invested company, attach the foreign investment registration certificate. A non-resident director must ensure the entity has a valid Korean tax identification number; otherwise, the return will be rejected, late-filing penalties will apply, and treaty benefits may be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 법인명 및 대표자 (Corporate Name and Representative)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the exact registered Korean legal name and the representative director's identification. For foreign directors, enter the passport number and country of issuance. Failure to correctly identify a Korean resident director for service of process may trigger audit and penalty procedures.

Enter the registered head office and production facility address in Korea. If located in a Free Economic Zone or Foreign Investment Zone, include the applicable zone code and certificate reference, since preferential rates and exemptions must be substantiated with the relevant approval documents.

Report all gross revenue from sales of silicone fidget toys and digital content, net of VAT. Export sales must be supported by customs declarations. Intercompany revenue with foreign affiliates must be reported at arm's length prices and separately disclosed in the international transaction statement (Form No. 121).

Include cost of raw silicone, molds, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead. If raw materials are purchased from a related foreign supplier, the price must satisfy the arm's length standard and be consistent with the customs valuation. Under-reporting revenue through offshore payment platforms is a common criminal trigger.

SG&A deductions must be ordinary, necessary, and properly documented. Management or royalty fees paid to non-residents are deductible only if a valid service was rendered, the fee is at arm's length, and the overseas recipient has substance. Foreign service fees attract 22% withholding tax (20% + 2% local income tax) unless reduced by a DTA, with procedural disclosure required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 판매비와 관리비 (Selling, General and Administrative Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute operating income as Box 5 minus Box 6 and Box 7. If the entity consistently reports losses while generating revenue from digital exports or intercompany sales, the NTS may adjust income under the International Tax Adjustment Act.

Report interest income, FX gains, dividends from foreign subsidiaries, and other non-operating income. Any intercompany interest charged by a foreign parent must be tested against the arm's length rate and the thin capitalization ratio (2:1 general; 3:1 for financial institutions).

Report interest and FX losses. Interest payable to foreign related parties is subject to thin capitalization and Earnings Stripping rules. Excess interest that is non-deductible may be recharacterized as dividends, triggering dividend WHT.

Enter the taxable income as determined after statutory adjustments, including add-backs for non-deductible entertainment expenses, donations, and taxes. Attach the reconciliation schedule (세무조정계산서). Non-resident shareholders should note that any recharacterization by the NTS increases taxable income and may affect treaty relief.
Apply the progressive corporate tax rates: 9% (0-200M KRW), 19% (200M-20B), 21% (20B-300B), 25% (over 300B), plus 10% surtax over KRW 30B. Compute output tax before credits.

Claim statutory credits and reductions, including R&D credits, facility investment credits, foreign investment tax holiday, and free economic zone credits. Attach supporting schedules and certification. Credits must reflect actual qualifying activity performed in Korea.

Enter all prepaid taxes including interim payments, foreign tax credits, and withholding credits. Foreign tax credits are limited and must be calculated using the Korean foreign tax credit limitation formula. Attach Form No. 151 for foreign tax credits.

Calculate the final tax due or refund. If a refund is claimed, the NTS will review all cross-border transactions and may request additional documentation. A refund claim by a foreign-controlled entity is a high-risk trigger for transfer pricing audit.

Attach financial statements, auditor's report (if applicable), and all tax adjustment schedules. For entities with international transactions, attach the mandatory International Transaction Information Statement (Form No. 121). Foreign parent information must be disclosed on Schedule 20.

Confirm the electronic filing submission number from HomeTax. Keep a screenshot or PDF confirmation for 5 years. A foreign-controlled entity must also ensure its tax representative is appointed and registered with the NTS; absence of a tax representative is a procedural violation.

Complete the intercompany transaction disclosure in full. All related-party transactions exceeding KRW 500 million must be reported. For transactions exceeding KRW 5 billion, Local File and Master File must be prepared and submitted upon NTS request. Penalties for false or omitted statements are severe.

Dissection of cross-border payments by type. For each royalty, service fee, loan interest, and product sale, identify the related foreign counterparty, the transaction code, and the amount. Indicate if a DTA reduction is applied and attach the certificate of tax residence (Form No. 121-Schedule).
Provide the shareholding structure, foreign parent name, address, and tax ID. A false beneficial ownership statement may lead to denial of treaty benefits and criminal penalties.

For a foreign-owned Korean subsidiary, the NTS will examine accumulated profits. If retained earnings exceed reasonable working capital needs and no dividend is paid while the entity enjoys tax incentives, the NTS may apply the accumulated earnings tax for personal holding companies under the Corporate Tax Act (Article 56 and Personal Holding Company Rules).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: If the return is filed after the statutory deadline: (i) late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax for general ommissions; (ii) if no tax is paid, additional 0.022% per day late payment surcharge on the amount due; (iii) for false or fraudulent returns, 40% of the understated tax; (iv) for non-filing of international transaction disclosure, 30% of the understated tax or 5% of the transaction amount (max KRW 100 million), plus criminal liability under the International Tax Adjustment Act; (v) corporate tax evasion over KRW 300 million triggers criminal investigation under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 50 million per false transaction; (vi) failure to withhold or pay withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest and royalties results in liability for the unpaid tax, a 10% negligence penalty, and 0.022%/day late surcharge, and may be assessed personally against the responsible representative or director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national dividend withholding tax + 2% local income tax surtax on the dividend withholding tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of the jurisdiction where it is tax resident, showing the effective date of residency; (2) submit a TRC certified by the competent authority and, where required, a notarized Korean translation; (3) file a DTA withholding rate application (Form No. 121-1, 외국법인 국내원천소득에 대한 조세조약 제한세율 적용 신청) with the payer before or at the time of distribution, or in the absence of that, file a refund claim with the NTS within 5 years; (4) provide a declaration that the shareholder is the beneficial owner and has no obligation to pass the income on to a third party, is not a conduit, and satisfies the limitation-on-benefits clause (LOB) in the relevant DTA; (5) submit evidence of actual substantial business activity in the treaty country (employee count, premises, contracts, business purpose); (6) where Korea's DTA contains a principal purpose test under the MLI, demonstrate that obtaining treaty benefits was not the main purpose of the structure; (7) the Korean payer must withhold at the statutory rate unless the application is accepted, and any excess may be reclaimed by the non-resident by filing a refund request with supporting documentation. The beneficial ownership assessment will review whether the shareholder retains the right to use and dispose of the dividend, bears risk, and is not a 24-hour shell.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 500 million (approximately USD 375,000) for annual international transaction disclosure (Form No. 121). KRW 5 billion for mandatory Local File and Master File preparation. KRW 10 billion for Country-by-Country Report filing and notification. These thresholds apply per transaction type or aggregate related-party transactions, depending on the attachment schedules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime like BVI/Cayman, but applies a substance-over-form doctrine under corporate tax law and anti-avoidance principles. Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, transactions with no genuine business purpose or with a foreign shell entity may be disregarded. The Korean entity must have substantial employees, premises, and operational control of manufacturing and marketing activity to avoid the NTS attributing income to the foreign parent. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) include product design, manufacturing quality control, inventory management, supply-chain decision-making, and financial responsibility. A Yuhan Hoesa that is a mere pass-through without CIGA in Korea will be attacked, its intercompany pricing adjusted, and the entity may be deemed to have a foreign permanent establishment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Environmental / Product Safety Violation (Food-Grade Silicone Compliance)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing or producing silicone fidget toys using industrial-grade silicone, using chemical plasticizers or softening agents that exceed Korea's Food Sanitation Act and Korean Standards (KS) migration limits for food-contact materials, or failing to obtain Korea Conformity Label (KC) verification under Regulation on Safety Verification for Children's Products (RSC), since fidget toys are classified as children's goods subject to mandatory safety management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Children's Product Safety Special Act, a manufacturer or importer failing to obtain safety certification is subject to imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million. If the product causes a safety accident, the fine is up to KRW 100 million or imprisonment up to 5 years. The Ministry of Environment's chemical control law (CCA) imposes fines for use of restricted substances of up to KRW 30 million per violation. The Korea Customs Service may confiscate shipments and impose customs delay penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts have pierced the corporate veil where directors were personally involved in the decision to source non-compliant materials. Directors could be held civilly liable for consumer injuries and punitive environmental damage. Criminal liability: a director who intentionally manufactured with non-food-grade silicone faces imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of KRW 50 million. For repeat or gross negligence offenses, the punishment increases by half. The NTS may also recommend denial or revocation of export/import license, and the director faces personal injury tort liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting international online platform sales, keeping two sets of accounting books, failing to record cash sales, overstating deductible costs with fabricated invoices from foreign shell suppliers, using undisclosed foreign bank accounts, or misreporting intercompany revenue to shift profit offshore to a subsidiary or parent in a low-tax jurisdiction without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, omitting more than 30% of total revenue or underreporting net taxable income by more than KRW 50 million constitutes tax evasion, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 100 million. Additionally, the NTS imposes a 40% unfaithful return penalty on the understated tax, plus late payment surcharge of 0.022%/day. If the evasion exceeds KRW 300 million, the criminal penalty is up to 10 years imprisonment and fines up to 3 times the evaded amount. Habitual evasion increases the punishment to up to 10 years, and the corporate entity receives an additional penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the company is a shell or the director used the company to evade tax. The director is jointly liable for the unpaid corporate income tax, penalties, and surcharges. The court may order seizure of personal assets, bank accounts, and real estate of the director. Criminal liability: the director faces a sentence of up to 5 years imprisonment for intentional false reporting. For VAT evasion, similar imprisonment. Under Article 17 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, the director of a company evading corporate tax additionally faces a fine equal to 2 to 5 times the evaded amount. The NTS also requests prejudgment attachment of personal property. Non-resident directors who leave Korea may be subject to travel restriction (출국금지), red notice from Interpol, and extradition.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Structuring / Unregistered Foreign Financial Account
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving payments from overseas digital platforms into a foreign bank account without declaring the income to Korea, splitting payments to avoid tax reporting, failing to report the foreign account under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions, or structuring cash deposits to evade source identification. For a Yuhan Hoesa, transferring profits to a foreign parent without conducting proper WHT and without DTA beneficial ownership due diligence is also a red flag.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, any Korean law subject orKorean branch receiving foreign currency exceeding USD 5,000 equivalent must report the receipt. Non-reporting is subject to a fine of up to KRW 20 million. Under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions, false-name transactions attract fines up to KRW 15 million and imprisonment up to 3 years. The AML law (Act on Reporting and Using Information on Financial Transactions) imposes a fine up to KRW 100 million for failure to file suspicious transactions. In double tax avoidance structures, unreported cross-border dividends attract additional 20% WHT and the NTS may impose a 50% negligence penalty on unreported tax. The court can confiscate the foreign undeclared assets under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who control the bank accounts or direct the offshore payment channel are personally liable. Criminal liability for money laundering under the Criminal Act (embezzlement/breach of trust) can result in imprisonment up to 10 years for laundering proceeds from tax evasion. Under the Korean AML Act, a director who reports no suspicious transactions while controlling the flow can be fined up to 30 million and imprisoned up to 3 years. If the director is a foreign resident, the NTS may initiate mutual legal assistance to freeze accounts in the counterparty jurisdiction. Personal liability for unpaid taxes of up to 100% is imposed if the corporate veil is pierced. The director may also receive a travel ban and be banned from re-entry into Korea until the full amount of evaded tax is paid.
